system.name: RTOSUnit
system.one_liner: a configurable hardware acceleration unit that reduces context-switch latency and jitter in embedded real-time systems

components.name: RTOSUnit
components.role: hardware acceleration unit for context storing/loading and scheduling, accelerated via custom instructions

components.name: HW Scheduler
components.role: hardware-maintained ready/delay list scheduler (detailed in Figure 5)

components.name: Store FSM
components.role: asynchronously stores the previous task's context to memory in the background after an interrupt (b)

components.name: Restore FSM
components.role: loads a new task's context from memory into the register file and CSRs (f)

components.name: RISC-V Processor
components.role: generic host processor into which the RTOSUnit is integrated

components.name: Pipeline
components.role: the host processor's instruction pipeline; entered via ISR on interrupt

components.name: Memory Interface Arbitration
components.role: arbitrates the single memory port between the processor and the RTOSUnit (g)

components.name: Regfile
components.role: register file region holding the duplicated application/ISR banks

components.name: RF1 (APP)
components.role: application register bank, connected to both the core and the RTOSUnit

components.name: RF2 (ISR)
components.role: duplicated interrupt-service-routine register bank, connected only to the core (d)

components.name: CSRs
components.role: mstatus, mepc, mcause control/status registers; not replicated since they need not be freed for the scheduler (c)

components.name: Memory
components.role: main memory storing saved task contexts

flows.what: ISR entry and custom/mret instruction signaling
asynchronous background write of the previous task's context (Write RF)
register-file write trace read for restore
restored context written back to the register file (Write RF)
read/write access to mstatus, mepc, mcause
bank switch between application and ISR register files
arbitrated access to the shared memory port

content.key_idea: RTOSUnit plugs into a RISC-V core as dedicated hardware (a scheduler plus store/restore FSMs) that duplicates the register file and arbitrates memory access, so context storing, loading, and scheduling can be offloaded from software to hardware via custom instructions.
content.reading_order: Left RTOSUnit block (scheduler, store/restore FSMs) first, then follow the lettered interface arrows right into the RISC-V processor's pipeline, duplicated register banks, and CSRs.

summary: This figure gives the proposed architecture overview of RTOSUnit, a configurable hardware unit that accelerates FreeRTOS context switching and scheduling on RISC-V cores. On the left, the RTOSUnit region holds a HW Scheduler (detailed in Figure 5) plus a Store FSM and Restore FSM that asynchronously save and load task context. On the right, a generic RISC-V Processor region shows the pipeline, a duplicated register file (RF1/APP and RF2/ISR banks joined by a sparse MUX for bank switching), and the CSRs (mstatus, mepc, mcause) the unit accesses; a Memory Interface Arbitration block shares the single memory port between processor and unit. Per the caption, green marks components RTOSUnit adds and yellow marks required processor changes, while lettered call-outs (a)-(g) key each wire to the mechanism it implements.
summary_zh: 该图为 RTOSUnit 的整体架构：左侧 RTOSUnit 含硬件调度器与存取上下文的 FSM，右侧 RISC-V 处理器展示流水线、复制的寄存器堆 RF1/RF2 与 CSR，字母标注对应实现细节，绿色为新增、黄色为处理器改动。
